claim_text: Combined power + gas circular debt reached Rs5.286 trillion by June 2026 up from Rs5.206 trillion at start of CY2026
source: The Nation citing an unnamed official source

claim_text: IMF's third EFF review and second RSF review estimated power circular debt at Rs1.764 trillion and gas circular debt at Rs3.442 trillion as of early 2026
source: The Nation citing IMF review documents

claim_text: Power sector circular debt stood at Rs1.675 trillion at end of FY2025-26 (June 30 2026) up from Rs1.614 trillion at end of FY2024-25 a net increase of Rs61 billion
source: The News citing Power Division data

claim_text: Gross power sector circular debt flow in FY2025-26 was Rs364 billion 709% higher than the prior year's Rs319 billion
source: Express Tribune

claim_text: FY2025-26 power debt growth drivers: DISCO inefficiencies Rs262bn; K-Electric non-payment Rs194bn; lower bill recovery Rs64bn; tariff/WAPDA invoice delays Rs63-75bn; interest Rs14bn
source: The News and Express Tribune cross-corroborating

claim_text: Government offset the gross flow with Rs302bn in subsidy payments Rs129bn loan principal repayment and Rs98bn unclaimed-subsidy reduction netting a Rs61bn increase
source: The News citing Power Division data

claim_text: K-Electric's outstanding receivables reached Rs421 billion by June 2026 (Rs197bn principal + Rs224bn accumulated markup)
source: The News citing Power Division data

claim_text: K-Electric's Rs194bn non-payment traces to a dispute with NEPRA over the Incremental Consumption Package implemented Nov 2020-June 2021 and extended July 2021-Oct 2023 now escalated to SIFC
source: Business Recorder via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: Gas sector circular debt stood at Rs3.611 trillion as of June 2026 up from Rs3.442 trillion at start of CY2026 (Rs1.839tn principal remainder late payment surcharges)
source: The Nation corroborated by multiple other outlets

claim_text: IMF requested that the circular debt flow be restricted to Rs300-325 billion lower than the prior year's level
source: Express Tribune via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: SNGPL's own circular debt/receivables burden reached Rs819 billion as of June 2026 attributed mainly to gas price freezes and RLNG diversion to lower-tariff domestic consumers
source: Express Tribune corroborated by Profit ProPakistani and EnergyUpdate

claim_text: SNGPL told the government it is unable to repay a Rs50 billion bank loan taken for LNG payments; government extended sovereign guarantee to June 2027
source: ProPakistani and EnergyUpdate via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: Gas sector circular debt has been accumulating since FY2013 driven by inadequate or delayed consumer price revisions; some improvement since November 2023
source: Express Tribune

claim_text: April-June 2026 indigenous gas diverted to RLNG-based power plants was charged at Rs2000/MMBtu instead of the notified RLNG price of Rs3498-4375/MMBtu; Petroleum Division warned this creates a revenue shortfall for SNGPL and hinders circular debt reduction
source: EnergyUpdate.com.pk

claim_text: Petroleum Division asked Power Division to submit a workable payment plan for SNGPL's receivables due June 30 2026 subject to reconciliation of outstanding amounts
source: EnergyUpdate.com.pk

claim_text: SNGPL's power-sector receivables were Rs148.5 billion in February 2025 Rs76.5 billion in August 2025 and Rs114.287 billion in December 2025 not moving in a simple straight line
source: Business Recorder Profit by Pakistan Today EnergyUpdate and HUM News via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: Reporting attributes SNGPL's power-sector receivables to inadequate fund releases by CPPA-G to the power sector which in turn delays payments to the gas utility
source: Business Recorder via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: August 2025 Rs76.5bn power-sector-to-SNGPL debt breakdown: Rs50.431bn WAPDA plants (Guddu Rs29.958bn Nandipur Rs16.615bn plus Muzaffargarh Faisalabad Shahdra); Rs18.119bn disputed gas charges; Rs31.462bn late payment surcharges; IPPs Liberty Power Rs16.397bn Orient Power Rs1.441bn Engro Energy Rs424 million
source: Business Recorder EnergyUpdate and HUM News via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: Liberty Daharki Power Limited owed SNGPL Rs20.029 billion as of December 9 2025 (Rs17.812bn gas arrears + Rs2bn unpaid upfront + additional instalments) exceeding its Rs3.085bn cash security deposit; SNGPL threatened gas supply suspension
source: Profit by Pakistan Today and Business Recorder via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: LDPL stated it could not pay because of limited payments received from the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA-G)
source: Business Recorder via WebSearch synthesis only

claim_text: LDPL previously served a force majeure notice under its PPA reported March 2023 after SNGPL suspended gas supply over a payment dispute; a prior October 2021 PPA Amendment Agreement had established non-supply of gas by SNGPL as an Other Force Majeure Event
source: Business Recorder via WebSearch synthesis only chronology appears inconsistent

claim_text: Government developed a Gas Circular Debt Management Plan via Petroleum Division Task Force on Power Reforms and KPMG presented to IMF in March and May 2026 expected to roll out in FY27
source: Profit ProPakistani and EnergyUpdate via WebSearch synthesis only

source: via WebSearch synthesis only

source: Express Tribune via WebSearch synthesis only
